9 March, 2000 (Fagan Sud 3, V.S. 2056) Khedbrahma, Gandhinagar

This morning Swamishri had a 102° fever. With the prevailing weakness and temperature Swamishri still suggested that he visit Modasa two days later. But at the suggestion of senior sadhus Swamishri agreed to return to Gandhinagar for treatment and complete rest.
At 5.40 p.m. Swamishri left Himatnagar and arrived at 7.05 p.m.
1 March, 2000 Ahmedabad

"The Joy of Shastriji Maharaj" Swamishri was in Ahmedabad. After having darshan of Yogiji Maharaj's murti in a shrine in the mandir pradikshana, a devotee asked Swamishri, "Bapa, there is so much joy on your face. What is the reason for this joy?" Swamishri replied spiritedly, "The joy of Shastriji Maharaj!" Swamishri's unbroken joy arises out of his profound realisation and attachment to Lord Swaminarayan and his guru.

A Tulsi Plant: Yesterday, Swamishri was welcomed and honored with a pot of Tulsi plant during an inaugural function of an MRI machine at the Civil Hospital. This morning Swamishri asked a sadhu where he had placed the pot of Tulsi plant. "In your room," the sadhu replied. "See to it that it is planted in an appropriate place in the mandir grounds. They have presented it with great love and affection. And besides leaving the plant there it will dry up and die by itself." In the least overwhelmed by the presentation (Tulsi Plant) as a mark of honor, Swamishri's hallmark of care and affection is reflected by his appreciation and recognition of the officials' sentiments. Swamishri's care and concern that a plant should not dry up and die also shows his respect and love for the survival of plants.
12 March, 2000 Gandhinagar Sunday Assembly

Despite physical weakness due to illness, Swamishri expressed a wish to go to the Sunday assembly this evening. When Swamishri entered the assembly, he was welcomed by thunderous clapping from the devotees. After Thakorji's darshan, Swamishri sat on a sofa and listened to the spiritual discourse for a half hour. When the discourse concluded at 7.30 p.m., Swamishri returned to his residence and said, "I have obeyed Yogiji Maharaj's instruction (by attending the Sunday assembly). We had the opportunity of having the darshan of the devotees and in pleasing them." Even in such a debilitated state Swamishri obeyed to the wish of Yogiji Maharaj by attending the Sunday discourse.
By washing two tons of soil one gets only a pinchful of pure gold, likewise, God and His holy sadhu discourse to thousands and only five become dedicated.

At 9.35am, Swamishri arrived at Raisan and amidst Vedic chantings inaugurated the BAPS cattle camp with Shri Keshubhai Patel the Chief Minister of Gujarat. During an assembly, the Chief Minister lauded the activities inspired by Swamishri, "The unique attribute of this cattle camp is that there are no paid persons serving here... One finds dedication and feelings here, and that is why the work done here is proper and organized." Finally, Swamishri blessed the function, emphasizing the need to serve cattle because of their services to us. After the function, Swamishri individually blessed the farmers who, owned the drought-afflicted cattle, had come to offer their services in the camp. Before departing, Swamishri visited the cattle camp and enquired in detail about the arrangements for the cattle.
Swamishri departed from New Delhi in the afternoon and arrived in Atladra by evening.

At 6.30 pm Swamishri arrived in Mahelav. First he went for darshan at Shastriji Maharaj’s birthplace. After darshan, Swamishri chanted dhun for the successful completion and inauguration of Akshardham in New Delhi, centenary celebration of BAPS in 2007, etc. Thereafter Swamishri went for darshan of the shrine where Dungar Bhagat had narrated the Mahabharat. After reaching the mandir Swamishri blessed the devotees gathered for a satsang assembly.

Swamishri was in Vidyanagar. As devotees filed past for his blessings, Swamishri called a youth back. He was a farmer from a village of Charotar district. “I have heard,” Swamishri began, “that you are extravagant in your spendings. Is that true?” The youth remained silent. So on his behalf a sadhu revealed, “He is always experimenting in farming. Till now he has failed in most of them and lost lots of money.” “What crops do you sow?” Swamishri enquired. “Tomatoes and ladyfingers,” he replied. “Did you get any profit?” “No. I suffered a loss.” Like a seasoned counsellor and patriarch Swamishri advised, “Farm only those products that you have been doing for years and in which you have experience. If rice and wheat grow well, then sow them but do not try vegetables. There is no need to lose your money unnecessarily. Work hard. If you need a well then it is worth spending money for it. But you have to think again when your experiments yield you nothing. “Your brother sends you money from America, but from your fertile land of Charotar, decide for yourself that you do not have to ask for any more money from him. Keep this in mind.”

A satsangi student, Kashyap Pandit, residing at the BAPS hostel in Vidyanagar offered Swamishri his hand in promise. He asked, “You have fulfilled your promises to us. But today, tell me what promise do you want from me.”
“As a promise I want your allegiance to satsang and your steadfastness in following moral injunctions. Be very vigilant that you never fall into addictions, vices and bad company.”
Swamishri expects no mundane promises from us. He solely wishes for the moral and spiritual elevation of all.
Swamishri performed the pratishtha rituals of pujan and arti of murtis for the BAPS hari mandir in Bhoj (Vadodara).

To please Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj children, youths and senior devotees perform austerities, pilgrimages or other devotional means. The spiritual endeavors performed by the devotees during Swamishri's visit to the local centers are congratulatory and worthy of recognition. It also reflects Swamishri's divinity for inspiring such spiritual efforts in children, teenagers and devotees.

Swamishri came into the mandir. Today Harikrishna Maharaj was dressed in tribal attire. The pujari Yogimangal Swami had learned to tie a tribal style turban from Varsingbhai of Dahod. After darshan of Harikrishna Maharaj standing in tribal dress with that kind of turban, Swamishri said, "Does a tribal person hold something like an axe in his hand?"
"No, they carry a bow and arrows, but those were not here, so we placed an axe," the sadhus explained.
Swamishri knows the particular features of each people. And everyone saw once more how fine his eye is when doing darshan.
